headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow only if ChatGPT Desktop ingests shared content; otherwise the pair is mostly non-interacting and low-risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and app content, so it could ingest attacker-controlled text if the user bridges it manually. The zoomcamp profile is a non-runnable course repo with no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented automatic channel from B into A. This is a manual-copy pathway, not a default one.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-derived text into ChatGPT Desktop or opens B files in a supported app context, injection becomes possible.
IF no content from B is ever pasted, uploaded, or screen-captured into A, the pathway does not activate.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for this workflow.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before pasting any B output into A.
Keep B materials in read-only form and avoid opening them in supported apps.
Add a one-line instruction to ignore embedded directives in imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, but B is a non-runnable course with no declared data classes or I/O surfaces. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated data plane between them, so leakage is limited to manual transfer of user-provided content into A. B itself does not expose a leak path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded to A while also being copied into B-related notes, those contents can be exposed in A outputs.
IF B is used only as a static course reference, no cross-agent leakage pathway is present.
mitigations: Avoid uploading sensitive files to A when working on B materials.
Separate B notes from any confidential project workspace.
Redact identifiers before sending content to A.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive sample dataset for B exercises.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace segregation between course notes and private files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, while B is not runnable and has no declared write or network capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair in default use.
conditions: IF B is replaced with a runnable agent that writes to the same directory as A, conflict risk would change.
IF A is granted write or git privileges outside the profile, this verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep A in read-only mode for this workflow.
Do not pair A with a writable agent on the same repo.
Review any future B runtime before enabling it.
Use separate directories for analysis and editing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate analysis from files and app context, but B is a course artifact rather than an action-taking agent, so there is no documented downstream automation. Any cascade would require the operator to treat A's output as authoritative and then manually apply it to B-related work. That is a limited, human-mediated pathway.
conditions: IF the operator uses A's output as the sole source of truth for B-related decisions, errors can propagate.
IF B is later wrapped in an automated pipeline that consumes A output, cascade risk increases.
mitigations: Verify A outputs against the original B source material.
Require a second human review before acting on A-generated conclusions.
Keep A outputs clearly labeled as draft assistance.
Avoid using A output as input to any automated B workflow.
requires-engineering: add validation checks before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code under OpenAI's desktop product, while B is an open-source course with no declared data handling or residency commitments. The pair does not document a shared regulated-data flow, so compliance risk is mainly from the operator placing regulated data into A while using B materials. B is not cited for a residency mismatch because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into A during B-related work, the operator must ensure A's handling meets the applicable policy.
IF B is used only for public course content, no compliance breach is indicated by the profiles.
mitigations: Do not use regulated data in this pair without a policy review.
Keep B exercises on public or synthetic data.
Check retention settings before uploading any files to A.
Document the data class used for each session.
requires-engineering: map the workflow to a formal compliance control set.
